answer: Standing is a river that only counts when it flows outward and never circles back: an identity earns standing when its work flows to strangers outside its own circle — they use it, build on it, or pass it on — and a jetty of trust only holds when the river keeps flowing outward, like a fable that only rings true when strangers retell it. A farm of a thousand fakes has no river: its work only circles among its own members, so each fake must produce work that strangers outside its farm genuinely use — and one circular flow wipes what it claimed.
